facts.text: Corte Madera’s name comes from the Spanish command “chop wood,” reflecting the town’s historic redwood lumber industry.
The Pixley family founded Corte Madera’s first subdivision, helped build downtown, and launched the famed San Francisco magazine The Argonaut.
In 1898 Jerry Adams opened the town’s first hotel and tavern just south of the train station, sparking local commerce.
Wilfred George’s generosity in 1998 earned Corte Madera a Victorian bandstand, the Piccolo Pavilion, at Old Square’s heart.
Railroad Park, founded in 1916 and preserved by the Women’s Club, lies in the northwest quadrant of the old train station square.
In 1980 Corte Madera merged its police force with Larkspur’s, creating the Twin Cities Police Authority that later joined San Anselmo in 2013.
